# x0x-reference: dinsync.info TB-303 reference recordings

<!-- Generated by tools/x0x_reference_manifest.py from "x0x-reference knob positions.txt" and the WAV files. Do not edit by hand. -->

Source: <http://www.dinsync.info/2010/02/tb-303-reference-recordings-for-x0xb0x.html> (copied into `x0x-reference knob positions.txt`).

A single hardware TB-303 recorded with a systematic sweep of every front-panel knob. Knob positions are the author's approximate settings ("these are analog knobs"). **Levels are not normalised** -- not within a set and, as the repeated settings below show, not across sets either -- so absolute level differences (e.g. accented vs. unaccented, low vs. high cutoff) are part of the reference.

Machine-readable version: [`x0x_reference_manifest.json`](x0x_reference_manifest.json) (read by `tools/calibrate_reference.py --manifest`).

## File layout

- 25 files `SET-A1.wav` ... `SET-E5.wav`, 44100 Hz, 16-bit stereo (L and R are identical to within -60 dB; use their mean), 49.1 s each.
- 16 notes per file, one every 3 s. Note *n* (1-based) sits in the slot `[3(n-1), 3n)` s and its note-on is at `3(n-1) + 1.1368` s. The notes are on a fixed grid: an accented note starts sounding +0.0 ms from that point (std 2.0 ms), an unaccented one +4.5 ms (std 0.8 ms) -- at the moment the accented notes start, the unaccented ones show only a faint click and their VCA opens a few ms later. The grid note-on is therefore defined as where the accented notes start sounding.
- Every note is **C2** (the keypad's lowest C, no transpose; the 303's lowest note): measured 63.54-65.64 Hz, i.e. -50.1 to +6.1 cents from 65.406 Hz (median +5.3). The outliers are all strong resonance / Env Mod sweeps, whose moving resonant peak biases the harmonic fit. The oscillator itself is steady: the notes with Resonance and Env Mod <= 50 % agree within ~0.3 c per file, with file medians of +5.2 to +5.6 c (the D/E files have no such notes). Their overall median, +5.42 c, is the manifest's `render_tune_cents`.
- Gate (note-on to gate-off) 1320-1341 ms (median 1330 ms); the release has died into the noise (~-88 dBFS) well before the next slot.
- The 16 notes are 4 knob **positions** x 4 notes:

| Note in file | Position | Waveform | Accent |

| 1 | 1 | saw | no |
| 2 | 1 | saw | yes |
| 3 | 1 | square | no |

## Knob settings per set

Each row of a set is one position; the knob that the set sweeps is in **bold**. The rows (A-E) set the level of the four fixed knobs (A: 0 %, B: 25 %, C: 50 %, D: 75 %, E: 100 %); the column (1-5) says which knob is swept (1 Cutoff, 2 Resonance, 3 Env Mod, 4 Decay, 5 Accent). In row A the swept knob starts at 25 % while the others stay at 0 %; in rows B-E it sweeps 25-100 %, so one position repeats the row's base setting.

## Per-note ranges and measurements

Times in seconds from the start of the file. *Slot* is the note's full 3 s window; *Note-on* is the grid note-on; *Sound* is when the note becomes audible (ms after note-on); *Gate-off* is measured from the audio (the steepest fall of the one-period RMS envelope); *Clip* is the window the calibrator compares (50 ms before note-on, 1.75 s long). Levels in dBFS (mean of L/R): *RMS* over the sustained part (50 ms after note-on to 20 ms before gate-off), *Peak* over the slot.
